newsitem.title: USA: Tropical depression hovers over Caribbean.
newsitem.headline: Tropical depression hovers over Caribbean.

text.p: A tropical depression remained stalled off the northeast coast of Nicaragua on Tuesday and was expected to soon strengthen into Tropical Storm Marco, the National Hurricane Center said.

At 4 a.m. EST (0900 GMT), the center of the depression was located 125 miles (200 km) east-southeast of Cabo Gracias a Dios, a small city located near Nicaragua's border with Honduras, forecasters said.
The depression was stationary and was centered at latitude 14.4 north and longitude 81.0 west.
The depression had maximum sustained winds of 35 mph (55 kph), and was expected to strengthen during the day.

If its sustained winds top 39 mph (62 kph), the depression will become Tropical Storm Marco, the 13th in a series of named storms during this year's Atlantic hurricane season. A tropical storm graduates to hurricane status when its maximum winds exceed 74 mph (119 kph).
Computer models indicated the depression was likely to eventually move to the northeast, dumping heavy rain on Jamaica, eastern Cuba and Hispaniola.
